outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the inequality has been claimed proved in every dimension by OpenAI (Astra, announced 1 August 2026, with a Lean 4 formalisation whose declaration matches the bullet and which the repository's manifest reports as sorry-free), and a separate arXiv preprint by Jihao Liu (2 August 2026) claims the equality case and states that together with OpenAI's inequality it completes the conjecture; an undated PDF hosted on Anthropic's CDN claims the inequality by a complex-analytic route; a human audit (Sienicki and Sienicki, 3 August 2026, revised to v3 9 September 2026) found the analytic Chapter 8 'verification incomplete' with no confirmed error; no peer review of any of these was found; a 2022 unrefereed preprint claims the bound fails in high dimensions.
problem_asks: Read from the January 2024 bullet alone. Part A (the bullet's assertion): for every dimension n (the Lean declaration takes n > 0), every convex body K in R^n (compact, convex, with nonempty interior, which the bullet implicitly requires for an interior lattice point to exist) that contains exactly one lattice point of Z^n in its interior, and whose centre of mass (barycentre) is that lattice point, satisfies vol(K) <= (n+1)^n/n!. This is a single assertion of an upper bound; the bullet does not state an equality clause. Part B (not in the bullet's wording, but part of the conjecture as the literature states it, e.g. Nill and Paffenholz 2014, MathWorld): equality holds only when K is a unimodular image of the centred simplex (n+1)Delta_n - (1,...,1), where Delta_n = conv{0, e_1, ..., e_n}. Recorded separately so the later pass can see which part each event reaches. Reduction note: translating by a lattice vector preserves the lattice-point hypothesis, so the bullet's 'centre of mass is the lattice point' is equivalent to 'barycentre 0 and unique interior lattice point 0', which is the form used in the Lean statement.

events.what_happened: Eugene Ehrhart stated the bound as a conjecture in a Comptes Rendus note (C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 258, 4885-4887, 1964; reference as given by MathWorld and Wikipedia). The special cases of dimension 2 and of simplices in every dimension are attributed to Ehrhart in the literature (Wikipedia lead; Nill and Paffenholz 2014; MathWorld). I did not read Ehrhart's own papers; Wikipedia's reference list cites a 1967 Crelle paper by Ehrhart alongside the 1964 note, and I could not tell which contains the special-case proofs.
events.delivers: The inequality (Part A) for n = 2 and for simplices in all dimensions, per secondary sources. Restricted to those two classes. Equality clause (Part B): not established by these results.
events.remains: Part A for all other convex bodies, all n >= 3 except simplices. Part B in general.
events.doubts: The year of the special-case proofs is not pinned down by my sources; the 1964 date is for the conjecture statement and may not be the date of the dimension-2 and simplex proofs.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: proves the upper bound in the special cases.
events.object: The sharp example is the centred simplex (n+1)Delta_n - (1,...,1): it has centroid 0, no other interior lattice point, and volume (n+1)^n/n!, so the bound is attained (as stated by Wikipedia, MathWorld and Nill and Paffenholz). This is the classical extremal body, not a new object.

events.what_happened: Theophilus Agama, 'The Ehrhart volume conjecture is false in sufficiently higher dimensions in R^n', posted to AfricArXiv (not arXiv), DOI 10.14293/111.000/000027.v1, issued 27 May 2022 (accessioned 24 March 2024). The record's abstract (truncated, as fetched) says that using the method of compression the author shows the volume of a ball K in R^2 with a single interior lattice point at its centre of mass satisfies a lower bound; the bound itself is cut off on the page. The full PDF ('Erharht volume conjecture.pdf', 300.53 KB) was not accessed.
events.revisions: Single version v1 on the record. Agama's separate arXiv paper 1912.08075 (The Compression method and applications) has 13 versions up to 24 March 2026, but its abstract does not mention Ehrhart (see dead_ends).
events.delivers: Claims that Part A fails: a ball with a unique interior lattice point at its centre of mass has volume above (n+1)^n/n! in high dimensions. The claimed counterexample's dimension and bound are not verified; the record is internally inconsistent (title says high-dimensional R^n; fetched abstract says R^2).
events.remains: Nothing is settled by this preprint; if correct, it would refute Part A.
events.doubts: (1) The record calls itself a preprint and says it has not been peer-reviewed. (2) Internal inconsistency: the title says high dimensions in R^n, the fetched abstract says R^2, and the conjecture is proved in dimension 2 by Ehrhart, so an R^2 counterexample would contradict a proven case. (3) A search summary says the claimed lower bound is n^n/sqrt(n); if that were correct it would exceed the 4^n upper bound that follows from Milman-Pajor and Minkowski's first theorem (taken from search summaries of Nill and Paffenholz; not checked against the primary sources). (4) No later paper found engages with it, and the OpenAI and Anthropic-hosted results (later events) claim the opposite.
events.direction: Against Part A: claims the bound fails in high dimensions.
events.object: A ball in R^n (abstract: R^2) with a single interior lattice point at its centre of mass, with a lower bound on its volume via compression. The bound and the dimension are not legible in the fetched record, so I cannot say what volume is claimed; the claim as titled is that the inequality fails for sufficiently large n.

events.what_happened: OpenAI announced on 1 August 2026 a set of ten results in mathematics and theoretical computer science produced by an internal, unreleased version of its model 'Astra', published as a report, 'Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science' (MathWorld cites its Chapter 8, 'The Sharp Inequality in Ehrhart's Volume Conjecture', dated 1 August 2026, at cdn.openai.com/pdf/ten-proofs-oai.pdf). The result is listed in the announcement as 'Ehrhart's volume conjecture' and, per the repository README, as 'The sharp maximum volume in every dimension for a convex body whose centroid is its only interior lattice point'. Lean 4 certificates for all ten results are in github.com/openai/ten-proofs; the file EhrhartVolumeInequality.lean (main declaration ehrhart_volume_inequality_for_sets) carries publication_date 2026-08-01 in formalization.yaml. I could not open OpenAI's own page or the PDF (403 and unreadable binary), so the announcement's wording comes from secondary coverage quoting it.
events.revisions: Chapter 8 audit found by Sienicki and Sienicki (arXiv 2608.14673 v1 3 Aug 2026; v2 25 Aug 2026; v3 9 Sep 2026). The openai/math history.md records only the 7 October 2026 withdrawals of other manuscripts; no Ehrhart change recorded there (read only as far as its first and only dated entry).
events.delivers: Part A, as stated in the Lean declaration: for n > 0, every compact convex S in R^n with nonempty interior, barycentre 0 and interiorLatticePoints S = {0} satisfies normalizedVolume S <= ((n:R)+1)^n/n! (signature read verbatim from the raw file). This covers every dimension and the whole class of bodies in the bullet, subject to the definitions of normalizedVolume (not read) being Lebesgue volume, which the sharpness by the simplex makes likely. Part B is not delivered by this event.
events.remains: Part B (equality characterisation; delivered only by the separate Liu event). The Lean declaration encodes only the inequality (the file lists one main theorem and asymptotic Bergman-dimension lemmas near the top; I did not read the whole file).

events.what_happened: Jihao Liu, 'The equality case of Ehrhart's volume conjecture', arXiv:2608.01040 (sole author; v1 submitted 2 August 2026, v2 6 August 2026; math.CO, cross-listed math.AG and math.CV; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). Claims that every full-dimensional compact convex body in R^n with barycentre as its unique interior lattice point and volume (n+1)^n/n! is a unimodular image of (n+1)Delta_n - (1,...,1), i.e. the equality case. The abstract says this 'resolves the equality case of Ehrhart's volume conjecture, as a counterpart of the inequality part recently proved by OpenAI'. Per the fetched HTML summary, Remark 1.4 says 'Together with Theorem 1.2, Theorem 1.3 completes Conjecture 1.1', and the paper uses OpenAI's analytic half directly rather than reproving it. The arXiv comments field reads 'AI generated with essential human strategical idea input. Human verified. Version 2, no math change, references updated'.
events.revisions: v1 2 Aug 2026 06:54 UTC (37 KB); v2 6 Aug 2026 (38 KB, 'no math change, references updated'). Metadata date 7 Aug 2026.
events.delivers: Part B (equality characterisation) for all n, with the volume hypothesis at the bound: bodies attaining (n+1)^n/n! are unimodular images of the simplex. By the paper's own account (Remark 1.4 as relayed) it completes Part A and Part B together only with OpenAI's Theorem 1.2 (the inequality), which it cites, not reproves.
events.remains: Part A is not delivered by this preprint; it rests on the OpenAI event. The paper's own Remark 1.6 says it is 'possible that we have missed some related references in the literature'. Whether its equality proof depends logically on OpenAI's analytic half is not stated in what I could read.
events.doubts: (1) The main result was produced with generative AI by the author's own account (see ai field), and the arXiv comments say 'Human verified', which is the author's self-report, not an independent check. (2) The 'key human input' the paper records is an observation about the method of OpenAI's report relying on a 2018 reference (Fuj18 in the relayed text); the second half's 'mechanisms have no counterparts in the K-stability argument' (relayed). (3) The audit (arXiv 2608.14673 v3) states that Liu's follow-up 'does not verify the analytic proof of OpenAI's sharp inequality' and that progress on one does not settle the analytic transitions questioned in the other. (4) The 'dictionary' in Remark 1.5 is described by the paper as heuristic (relayed). (5) No third-party reading of this paper was found.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: the equality characterisation the conjecture asserts holds (extremal bodies are unimodular images of the simplex).

disputes.summary: Two claimed proofs of the inequality: OpenAI's Chapter 8 (announced 1 August 2026, Lean-formalised) and the undated, unattributed Anthropic-hosted PDF with a complex-analytic proof. Their order and independence are not established. Liu's paper credits the inequality to OpenAI.

Agama (AfricArXiv, 27 May 2022) claims the bound fails in high dimensions; OpenAI's 2026 Lean-formalised proof and the Anthropic-hosted PDF claim it holds. The Agama record is unrefereed, internally inconsistent about the dimension, and no reply was found.

summary: Searches covered the problem's name and alternate forms (Ehrhart's volume conjecture; the centroid/unique-interior-lattice-point form; the Lean declaration name), result words (proof, counterexample, bound, equality case, dimension 2, simplices), recent work including the arXiv listings and the Berman-Berndtsson and Nill-Paffenholz lines, and separately the AI search (OpenAI's August 2026 Astra announcement, the Anthropic-hosted PDF, the Liu preprint, the Danus system, Alpoge's reproduction post). The bullet asks for the inequality in every dimension; its equality clause is recorded separately as Part B. On Part A there is now a Lean-formalised claimed proof: the OpenAI Astra result, announced 1 August 2026, whose main declaration (read verbatim from the raw file) matches the bullet's hypotheses and conclusion in every dimension n > 0, and whose formalization.yaml reports sorry_count 0 and only the standard axioms. The formal statement is a faithful reading of the bullet subject to the definition of normalizedVolume (not read) and the lattice-translation modelling choice. Against this, the only human audit I found (Sienicki and Sienicki, arXiv 2608.14673; I read section 3.2 via an HTML summary) places Chapter 8, the analytic argument for this result, as 'verification incomplete, with possible unresolved proof gaps in the presentation', with two reports diverging (minor vs major revision) and no confirmed error. Secondary coverage says none of the ten results was peer reviewed as of the cutoff. On Part B, Liu's arXiv:2608.01040 (2 August 2026) claims the equality classification for all n, states that together with OpenAI's Theorem 1.2 it completes the conjecture, says the main result was generated by AI (GPT-5.6-sol, Fable 5 and the Danus system, with the Danus system credited with the first half and the complete proof), and records 'Human verified' in its comments; the audit says Liu does not verify OpenAI's analytic proof. An undated PDF on Anthropic's CDN claims Part A by a complex-analytic route; I could not read its body and could not establish its author, date or status. The 2022 Agama preprint claims Part A fails; it is unrefereed and internally inconsistent about the dimension. Pre-2024 work: Ehrhart's special cases (dimension 2, simplices); Berman-Berndtsson 2011 and 2012 (toric and rational-polytope class; Part A for a class, Part B via projective-space maximality in the toric case); Nill-Paffenholz 2012, published 2014 (Part B for the toric class). Close calls: whether the OpenAI Lean statement is the bullet's problem (I read the signature but not the normalizedVolume definition or the body, so the fidelity call is a human judgment); whether Liu's equality classification is independent of OpenAI's analytic half (the paper says it uses that half directly); and whether the Anthropic-hosted PDF is a second proof or a duplicate of the same route (unknown). AI involvement: the OpenAI result is credited by OpenAI to Astra, which generated the arguments and formalised them, with human staff compiling the manuscript; OpenAI's own page was not readable (403), so the basis quote is from secondary coverage quoting OpenAI. Liu's AI credits are in his own abstract and remark, which I read via a fetch summary. Alpoge's report that for Ehrhart 'both models found basically the exact same argument' is a second-hand lead and is not recorded as evidence of an Ehrhart argument by any particular system. Things I checked and ruled out: the October 2026 OpenAI withdrawals (Weil classes, Kuga-Satake, rational Hodge for K3 products) do not concern this result per coverage and per the openai/math history.md, which has no Ehrhart entry; Scientific American's 'most exciting claims' piece does not mention Ehrhart; Tao, DeepMind/AlphaEvolve and Bloom do not appear in connection with this result. The Wikipedia article (lead, last edited 12 September 2026 per a fetch summary) describes the August 2026 announcement as proving the inequality part, and is tagged as needing non-primary sources; MathWorld (updated 2 October 2026) cites OpenAI's Chapter 8 and says the equality classification remains open, which predates or ignores Liu's preprint.
competing_reading: Reading A (Part A settled, Part B settled by Liu): the inequality has a Lean-checked proof with no sorry and standard axioms, the formal statement matches the bullet, and the classification of equality cases by Liu completes the conjecture (Liu's Remark 1.4 as relayed). On this reading the problem is resolved since the window, with AI generating both halves. Reading B (not settled): the inequality rests on an AI-generated argument with no peer review, whose analytic chapter an independent audit found 'verification incomplete'; Lean establishes the formal statement only, whose fidelity (normalizedVolume, the modelling of the centroid) has not been independently checked; Liu's equality result depends on the same unverified analytic half and is self-described as 'human verified' by its author; the Anthropic-hosted PDF is an unattributed second route; and the 2022 Agama counterexample has never been answered. On this reading the bullet is open in Part A (unverified) and Part B (single-author, unrefereed).
what_would_settle_it: (1) A check of EhrhartVolumeInequality.lean by someone who reads the body and the normalizedVolume definition, and a Comparator run of ComparatorChallenges/F_EhrhartVolumeInequality.json. (2) A written expert verification of Chapter 8's analytic transitions (Bergman/Laplace asymptotics, limiting plurisubharmonic ray, slope passage, positivity hypotheses), or a reply to the audit's two reports. (3) Peer-reviewed publication or a named mathematician's public verification of OpenAI's Ehrhart result and of Liu's equality classification. (4) The author, date and venue of the Anthropic-hosted PDF, and whether its argument is the same route. (5) A reply to, or withdrawal of, Agama's 2022 claim, and a read of its full PDF to see the dimension and bound claimed. (6) The OpenAI primary page or PDF, to confirm the 1 August 2026 wording that I could only read through coverage.
